items.text: The file's three forms and how XML writes lists (section 3): the bindings say it, DESL only names them.
The layout and behaviour taken from Notion (section 6): DESL's `surface` names which types play which part, not how a host draws them.
items.reason: How the table, its headers, menus and cells are drawn in the host's theme and controls is rendering; the description names the parts the surface's members play.

items.text: Conversions beyond their kind: what a written form is, that a multiple selection's names are joined by `, ` (section 8).
The steps that write two files and their atomicity (section 9): DESL requires it of a host, FBL keeps one history per body.
items.reason: One history entry whose undo restores both files' bytes is the host's undo stack; each file's edit is a splice of its own binding.

items.text: Relation values across files: a row of another file is a plain id here, resolved by the host, so its findings are the host's.
A parent cycle, which needs a recursive walk over values.
The view logic itself (how a filter, a sort and a grouping select and order rows): stated by the value types' comparisons and sorts and by section 5, and implemented by each host.
items.reason: Which rows a view shows and in what order is what the table draws; no conformance case compares a surface (ATD §2.3), and the stored view settings are the description's elements.

hostCode.behaviour: Setting a cell: an empty value or an unticked checkbox removes the cell, a value of a number, date, date and time or time that does not parse is refused in the type's words, and a new option typed in a selection's cell is made with a colour picked from its name.
A new view is named View, numbered when one has the name, and the file's active view is not changed.
Setting a condition's value writes the value under its property's type's key and removes any other.
The colour of an option made by typing it in a cell is picked from its name among the colours its property's options do not have yet.
hostCode.reason: The colour is the gesture's choice, which the host gives the operation setNewOption as its parameter colour.

hostCode.behaviour: A row that is its own ancestor through the parent relation is reported at its cell of that relation.
